clue.text: One in fifty used to be on night shifts

definitions.note: one of the fifty US states

parts.note: 'was' is the past tense of 'be', what used to be

indicators.note: things that shift move about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recalls once working the night shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'night shifts' looks like a work pattern, but 'shifts' is the anagram signal, working on ON NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States has fifty states and this north-western one is among them.

clue.text: A single query, hearing setters' favourite French city is Lyon?

definitions.meaning: a hit record (a single) whose title is a question: the Beach Boys song

definitions.text: hearing setters' favourite French city is Lyon?
definitions.meaning: a crossword setter told Lyon is the favourite would wish for the city of Nice instead, a city whose name doubles as the adjective

explanation.surface: A setter is asked which French city they like best and hears that it is Lyon.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading turns on Nice the Riviera city: setters love the pun on 'nice', so on hearing Lyon they would sigh for Nice instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1966 Beach Boys single whose title is phrased as a wistful question.

clue.text: Big game hunter who'd kill mice, by choice

indicators.note: one piece set beside another, so the two are joined

parts.note: choice as an adjective means excellent, first-rate
an owl is a night predator of mice

explanation.surface: A big-game hunter who would happily shoot mice, given the choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big game' looks like the hunter's quarry, but it is the definition: the American football final.
explanation.definitionFit: The championship match of American football is the biggest sporting game of the US year.

clue.text: Salt ten dead fish

parts.note: 10 written as the digits 1 and 0 looks like the letters I and O
D is an abbreviation for dead, as on family trees
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A grim recipe: salt ten dead fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like a verb telling you to cure the fish, but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical salt formed from iodine with another element, like potassium iodide.

clue.text: Permit daughter to carry electric motor?

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom piece carries what sits on top of it

parts.note: an electric vehicle is a green, environmentally friendly one
a motor is a car

explanation.surface: A parent lets their daughter take the electric car.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down entry, 'to carry' puts D at the bottom, holding up GREEN and CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The US document allowing a foreigner permanent residence and work is this card.

clue.text: Worked with a break two-thirds of the way through article

definitions.text: Worked with a break two-thirds of the way through
definitions.meaning: split 'Worked' after its fourth of six letters to get work plus -ed; work is an opus, OP, so this gives OP plus ED
an opinion piece printed opposite a newspaper's editorial page

explanation.surface: Someone worked through, with a break two-thirds of the way along.
explanation.walkthrough: Breaking 'Worked' two-thirds through leaves 'Work-ed'; OP (opus, a work) plus the ending ED, with the hyphen sitting at the break.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper opinion column, named for appearing opposite the editorial page.

clue.text: Negative number making the class sweat

parts.note: PE, physical education, is the school lesson that makes pupils sweat

explanation.surface: A refusal that makes the whole class sweat.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual American-style no, a negative reply.

clue.text: More inconvenience when late starting

indicators.note: late means gone, so the start of the word is gone

parts.note: a bother is an inconvenience

explanation.surface: Arriving late causes still more inconvenience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when late starting' drops the first letter of BOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean additional, as in 'some more people' or 'some further people'.

clue.text: Seabirds stop to relax on the coast north of Miami

indicators.note: one piece joined on to the next
the birds stop up, plug, the word for relax, sitting inside it

parts.note: to ease up is to relax
terns are seabirds
aboard means on a ship or train

explanation.surface: Seabirds pause to rest on the Florida coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stop' tells the birds to plug the word for relax; 'Seabirds' reads as the subject but is a piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic shoreline of the US runs from Florida up to Maine, north of Miami.

clue.text: Mums in fleeces wear dull swimwear with floats

indicators.note: the outer word wears the other like a garment, so it goes around it

parts.note: mat (matt) means dull, without shine
ewes are mother sheep in their woolly coats

explanation.surface: Mothers in fleece tops wear dull swimsuits with inflatables.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mae West is RAF slang for an inflatable life jacket, named after the buxom film star; 'wear' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The wartime inflatable life jacket kept airmen afloat, so it is swimwear fitted with floats.

clue.text: Gave a lift to Johnny coming back after uni

indicators.note: one piece placed after the other

parts.note: U is an abbreviation for university

indicators.note: coming back means read in the reverse direction

parts.note: Johnny Depp, the actor

explanation.surface: Someone drove the actor Johnny Depp home from university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' signals the reversal of the actor's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it, and both verbs are in the past tense.

clue.text: Delicate sensors say eel writhes before she wriggles

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second
a writhing creature twists about, so these letters are rearranged
something that wriggles squirms around, so this short word is rearranged

explanation.surface: An eel twists while a woman squirms, both sensing something delicately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writhes' rearranges SAY EEL into EYELAS; 'wriggles' rearranges SHE into HES.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine hairs fringing the eyelids react to touch and dust, warning the eye to blink.

clue.text: Ridiculing the Camptown races?

parts.note: the song Camptown Races writes 'the' in dialect as 'de'
horse races are riding events

explanation.surface: Mocking the old minstrel song Camptown Races.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Foster's song 'Camptown Races' has lines like 'de bob-tail nag' and 'de race track'; its 'de' supplies the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking and scorning someone, a synonym in the same -ing form.

clue.text: Curl first shot around edge of wall

indicators.note: the outer word goes around the inner letter

parts.note: in tennis the serve is the first shot of a point

indicators.note: the edge of the word means its first letter here

explanation.surface: A footballer curls their first shot round the edge of the defensive wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts W, from 'edge of wall', inside SERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball that curls in flight bends sideways, the same as veering off line.

clue.text: A file possibly left behind on top of everything

indicators.note: behind sends the left abbreviation to the back, after the other piece

parts.note: too means besides, on top of everything else

explanation.surface: A computer file got left behind as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' places L after TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A file is an example of a hand implement, one used for smoothing, so 'possibly' flags it.

clue.text: Bill withdrawing denial about young woman, one?

definitions.note: a noun phrase: the act of taking back a denial

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advert, AD
a miss is a young woman
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A bill withdrawing a denial about a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like the bill in the surface, but it is AD; ON (about) comes last though it is read early.
explanation.definitionFit: Confessing is the reverse of denying, so a confession takes back an earlier denial.

clue.text: Humorist's place for shopping cart (not back of Waitrose)

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', a link joining definition to wordplay, so the definition is the bare noun Humorist

indicators.note: not means leave this letter out

parts.note: a market is a place for shopping

indicators.note: the back of the word means its last letter

parts.note: a wain is a farm cart

explanation.surface: A shopping trolley in the supermarket Waitrose is missing its back.
explanation.walkthrough: Waitrose is a British supermarket chain; 'not back of Waitrose' removes E from MARKET.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Tom Sawyer is America's most famous comic writer.

clue.text: The one Fiat a Roman insurer provides retrospective cover for

indicators.note: looking back, so the letters are read backwards
the words provide the letters from within themselves
the outer words cover the letters inside them

explanation.surface: An Italian insurer gives backdated cover for a Fiat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provides ... cover for' lifts letters from inside FIAT A ROMAN IN, and 'retrospective' reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A beloved woman, the person someone calls their one true love.

clue.text: Big shot who married Mrs Simpson, united on third of June

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: Homer is Marge Simpson's husband in The Simpsons

indicators.note: the third letter of the word

explanation.surface: The man who married Wallis Simpson in June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mrs Simpson' suggests Wallis Simpson, who married Edward VIII in June 1937, but the husband here is cartoon Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball a hit that lets the batter round all bases is the biggest hit.

clue.text: Big ask short term saves shaky dollar

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it inside, so one piece holds the other
short means lose the last letter
shaky means unsteady, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A short-term loan to prop up a shaky dollar is a big ask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the last letter, 'shaky' is the anagram signal and 'saves' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a demanding request that will be hard to fulfil.

clue.text: Where degrees are taken by wallies, every so often

indicators.note: only some letters are taken at regular intervals, every second one

explanation.surface: Degrees taken by idiots, now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally is British slang for a fool. Take every second letter of BY WALLIES.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ivy League university in Connecticut, a place to study for a degree.

clue.text: Give substance to English doctor, oddly prescribing itself

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

indicators.note: the word 'oddly' instructs its own treatment: take its odd letters

explanation.surface: An English doctor strangely writes himself a prescription.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly prescribing itself' means take the odd letters of the word 'oddly': O, D, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To embody an idea is to make it concrete, to give it a physical form.

clue.text: Quite a sight, said the Statue of Liberty's builder

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, so we want its sound

parts.note: an eyeful is a striking sight

explanation.surface: Someone remarks what a sight the Statue of Liberty is.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustave Eiffel engineered the iron frame inside the Statue of Liberty before his Paris tower.

clue.text: You need some proof if this taken

definitions.text: You need some proof if this taken

indicators.note: some means part of these words, the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: If you take this you need proof.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the Fifth means refusing to testify under the US Fifth Amendment, which forces a prosecutor to find proof elsewhere; a fifth is also a bottle of spirits, measured in proof.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the Fifth is invoking the American constitutional right not to incriminate yourself.

clue.text: Grave after grave, first of two once dropped by America

definitions.text: Grave after grave, first of two once dropped by America

indicators.note: one piece put beside the next
one grave follows the other

parts.note: a tomb is a grave

indicators.note: dropped means removed, done just once, on one grave only

parts.note: a tomb is a grave

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Grave after grave: the result of the first of two weapons America once dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once dropped' removes T (the first letter of 'two') from the second TOMB, leaving OMB.
explanation.definitionFit: America dropped two of these nuclear weapons on Japan in 1945, Hiroshima the first.

clue.text: Critical of presenter always introduced before Dec 1

parts.note: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo, always named Ant first
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A TV presenter's show is critically due on 1st December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dec 1' looks like a date, but Dec is Declan Donnelly of Ant and Dec, the British TV duo, and 1 is I.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something means opposing or criticising it.

clue.text: Covers of unethical fanzine stirred up widespread complaint

indicators.note: stirred-up things are mixed about, so these letters are rearranged
the covers of a word are its outside letters

explanation.surface: The covers of an unethical fanzine caused widespread complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers of unethical' gives U and L; 'stirred up' rearranges them with FANZINE.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness is a complaint, and an epidemic of flu spreads widely.

clue.text: Nebraska tribesmen recalled eureka moment

indicators.note: called back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: eureka and aha are both cries of discovery
a mo is a moment

explanation.surface: Nebraskan tribesmen remembered a moment of discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses AHA MO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Omaha are a Native American people of Nebraska, which named its largest city after them.

clue.text: Environmentally friendly houses close to forty-ninth parallel

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: eco means environmentally friendly

indicators.note: close means end, so the last letter

explanation.surface: Eco-friendly houses near the 49th parallel, the US-Canada border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parallel' looks like part of the border latitude, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun meaning a close parallel or counterpart, as in 'an echo of the past'.

clue.text: Many amusements for kids sadly end in running riot

indicators.note: running riot means wild disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sadly the children's fun ends in a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: The California theme park holds countless rides and shows for children.
